children: A second federal judge has ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency under President
unlawfully canceled a $7 billion grant program aimed at expanding
US District Judge Tanya Chutkan in Washington on Tuesday
with Harris County, Texas, in finding that the EPA under its administrator, Lee Zeldin, exceeded its authority when it rescinded grants last year that had been previously awarded.
Congress had approved the $7 billion Solar for All grant program when it enacted Democratic President Joe Biden's signature climate investment law, the Inflation Reduction Act, in 2022.
Zeldin announced the termination of the program a month after Trump in July 2025 signed into law the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which eliminated the source of funding for the program.

Chutkan said the EPA's decision violated the Administrative Procedure Act because it rested on an incorrect reading of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which she said did not rescind already-obligated grant funds.

"Whatever the practical consequences of Congress’s rescission of unobligated administrative funds, they do not change the fact that Congress expressly chose to leave obligated grant funds undisturbed," she wrote in her decision.
Chutkan, an appointee of Democratic President Barack Obama, vacated the EPA's termination decision.
US District Judge Mary McElroy in Rhode Island last week also vacated the EPA's action on similar grounds.
The EPA says it is considering appealing both judges' decisions.
Harris County in 2024 was awarded a $249.7 million Solar for All grant.
The case is Harris County, Texas, v. Environmental Protection Agency, US District Court for the District of Columbia, No. 1:25-cv-03646.
For Harris County: Beth Neitzel, Emily Nash and Noah Shaw of Foley Hoag
For the EPA: Bethany Theriot, Tiffiney Carney and I-Heng Hsu of the US Justice Department
